scope: Corollary 5.8 (Upper fields on an intermediate projection) of the manuscript “The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture” (preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 022 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d91ccb7b68c5b0e2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an admissible realized table history and a row whose current projected grid is (z + aγ)/(Li/d), where I is the remaining prime-power part and a | I. On this grid the actual raw weight is bounded, after averaging static anchors, by a product of fields at the processed primes. Each nonconstant field lies in [0, 1]. At a full adaptive prime use the multiplier computed from the actual matching, extended by Rp where its prefix is unavailable; at a birth prime retain one active hard exclusion, or its prescribed scalar if none is active. An adaptive omission contributes only its residual scalar when a positive power remains. For every fixed choice of the static anchors, every subset of these fields has mean equal to the product of its ordinary local means. In particular the full upper product has mean Rdone(Li/d) := R (Li/I)/d  . The joint numerator period of any retained fields through a prime p divides the current projected denominator and is at most exp(O(p)), with the same fixed-parameter uniformity as in Proposition 5.7.
